input: What is the time complexity of binary search?
target: Binary search has O(log n) time complexity. It requires a sorted array and uses a divide-and-conquer approach by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.
Two Sum: Given an array and target, find two numbers that add to target. Use a hash map for O(n) solution.

input: How do I implement DFS on a graph?
target: DFS uses recursion or a stack. Mark visited nodes to avoid cycles. Time: O(V+E), Space: O(V)
React Hooks are functions that let you use state and effects in functional components. Common hooks: useState, useEffect, useContext.
REST uses HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and status codes (200, 400, 404, 500) for stateless, scalable APIs.

input: What's the difference between SQL and NoSQL?
target: SQL: structured, relational, ACID. NoSQL: flexible schema, document-based, scalable but eventual consistency.
Normalization removes redundancy through 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF stages. Each stage eliminates different types of dependencies.
ACID: Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (valid states), Isolation (concurrent independence), Durability (persistent).
Indexing creates data structures for faster lookups. Trade-off: faster reads but slower writes and more storage.
Merge sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm with O(n log n) complexity. Divide array in half, recursively sort, then merge sorted halves.
Hash table: data structure using hash function to map keys to values. Average O(1) lookup, O(n) worst case. Handles collisions with chaining or probing.
Tree traversals: Inorder (left-root-right), Preorder (root-left-right), Postorder (left-right-root), Level-order (BFS). Each has different applications.
DP: technique solving overlapping subproblems with optimal substructure. Use memoization to store solutions. Examples: Fibonacci, knapsack, coin change.
Quick sort: divide-and-conquer with pivot. O(n log n) average, O(n²) worst case. In-place, unstable. Practical choice for most cases.
BFS: explores graph level by level using a queue. Time O(V+E), Space O(V). Used for shortest path in unweighted graphs.
Linked list: nodes containing data and pointer to next. Insertion/deletion O(1), access O(n). Useful when frequent insertions needed.

input: What is a trie data structure?
target: Trie: tree for storing strings efficiently. O(m) search where m=string length. Space-efficient prefix storage. Used in autocomplete, spell checker.
JWT: JSON Web Token with header, payload, signature. Stateless auth. Token sent in Authorization header. Verify signature to ensure authenticity.
CORS: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing. Mechanism allowing requests from different domains. Uses headers: Access-Control-Allow-Origin, methods, headers.
Middleware: functions executing during request/response cycle. Use next() to pass control. Can modify request/response, end request, or call next middleware.
Closure: function with access to outer scope even after outer function closes. Inner function remembers variables from its lexical environment.
Event loop: continuously checks call stack and callback queue. If stack empty, moves callbacks from queue. Handles async operations, timers.
Promise: represents future value, pending/fulfilled/rejected state. Use .then() for success, .catch() for error. Chain promises or use async/await.
Async/await: syntactic sugar for promises. Await pauses execution until promise resolves. Cleaner than .then() chains. Must use try/catch for errors.
Flexbox: CSS layout model for 1D alignment. Use display: flex. Properties: justify-content, align-items, flex-direction, flex-wrap. Responsive by default.
CSS Grid: 2D layout system with rows and columns. display: grid. Place items using grid-template, grid-column/row. More powerful than flexbox for complex layouts.
Docker: containerization platform. Package app with dependencies in container. Isolated, portable, lightweight. Docker image + container runtime = deployment.
Kubernetes: orchestration platform for containers. Manages deployment, scaling, networking. Uses pods (smallest units), services, namespaces. K8s for production at scale.
CI/CD: Continuous Integration (automated testing on push) + Continuous Deployment (auto deploy to production). Pipelines: code → test → build → deploy. Tools: Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions.
Load balancing: distributes traffic across servers. Methods: round-robin, least connections, IP hash. Benefits: high availability, scalability, fault tolerance.
Caching: LRU, LFU, FIFO policies. TTL for expiration. Cache aside, write-through, write-behind patterns. Redis/Memcached for in-memory caching.
Sharding: horizontal partitioning across servers. Split by key range, hash, directory. Improves scalability but complex joins, uneven distribution issues.
Message queue: decouples services. Producer sends message, consumer processes. Examples: RabbitMQ, Kafka, SQS. Ensures reliability, scalability, async processing.
Microservices: independent services for each business capability. Benefits: scalability, flexibility. Challenges: complexity, network latency, distributed transactions.
API gateway: single entry point for microservices. Handles routing, auth, rate limiting, logging. Benefits: simplified client access, centralized control.
Replication: synchronizes data across servers. Master-slave, multi-master patterns. Improves availability, read performance. Trade-off: consistency, bandwidth.
Isolation levels: Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable. Higher levels prevent anomalies but reduce concurrency.
Optimization: use indexes, avoid full table scans, analyze execution plans. Techniques: index selection, join optimization, query rewrite.
ML: algorithms learn patterns from data. Supervised (labeled), unsupervised (unlabeled), reinforcement learning. Applications: classification, regression, clustering.
Neural networks: layers of neurons with weights. Forward pass: compute output. Backpropagation: update weights. Deep learning uses many hidden layers.
Overfitting: model memorizes training data, poor generalization. Prevention: regularization (L1/L2), dropout, early stopping, cross-validation.
Gradient descent: optimization algorithm minimizing loss. Update weights: θ = θ - α∇loss. Variants: SGD, momentum, Adam, RMSprop.
Cross-validation: splits data into k folds. Train on k-1, test on 1 fold. Repeat k times, average scores. Prevents overfitting, reliable evaluation.
Confusion matrix: TP, TN, FP, FN. Metrics: Precision, Recall, F1-score, Accuracy. Useful for imbalanced datasets.
Feature scaling: normalize features to same range. Standardization: (x-mean)/std. Normalization: (x-min)/(max-min). Important for distance-based algorithms.
Ensemble: combine multiple models. Techniques: bagging (Bootstrap Aggregating), boosting, stacking. Examples: Random Forest, Gradient Boosting. Better accuracy, reduced overfitting.
AWS: Amazon Web Services. Cloud platform offering compute (EC2), storage (S3), database (RDS), networking. Services: Lambda (serverless), DynamoDB, SQS, CloudFront.
EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud. Virtual machine in cloud. Choose: instance type, storage, security groups. Can scale up/down, pay-per-use.
S3: Simple Storage Service. Object storage for files, backups, static website. Cheap, durable, scalable. Key: bucket name + object key. Versions, lifecycle policies.
Lambda: Function as a Service (FaaS). Run code without managing servers. Trigger: API, S3, DynamoDB, schedule. Pay for execution time.
Git: version control system. Track changes, branches, collaborate. Commands: clone, add, commit, push, pull, merge. GitHub/GitLab for remote repositories.
Strategies: Git Flow (develop, main, features), GitHub Flow (main + features), Trunk-based (continuous deployment). Each suits different team sizes, release cycles.
SQL injection: attack inserting malicious SQL. Prevention: parameterized queries, prepared statements, input validation, stored procedures.
XSS: Cross-Site Scripting injection. Malicious script in webpage. Prevention: sanitize input, escape output, Content Security Policy headers.
CSRF: Cross-Site Request Forgery. Attacker tricks user to perform unwanted action. Prevention: CSRF tokens, SameSite cookies, verify origin header.
Buffer overflow: write beyond buffer bounds. Prevention: bounds checking, stack canaries, ASLR, safe languages (Rust), input validation.
OAuth: authorization framework enabling third-party access. User grants permission, gets access token. Flow: Authorization Code, Implicit, Client Credentials, Resource Owner Password.
Python: interpreted, high-level language. Uses: web (Django, Flask), data science (pandas, numpy), ML (TensorFlow, PyTorch), automation. Simple syntax, large ecosystem.
List: mutable, changeable, slower. Tuple: immutable, hashable, faster. Use tuple for fixed data, dictionary keys. List for dynamic collections.
NumPy: numerical computing library. Arrays, matrices, mathematical functions. Fast C backend. Foundation for pandas, scipy, data science libraries.
DataFrame: 2D table with rows/columns labeled. Read CSV (read_csv), filter, group (groupby), aggregate, pivot. Core pandas data structure.
List comprehension: concise way creating lists. Syntax: [x*2 for x in range(5)]. Faster, readable. Can add conditions: [x for x in list if x > 5]
Lambda: anonymous function. Syntax: lambda x: x*2. Use with map, filter, sorted. Limited to single expression.
Decorator: function wrapping another function. Modify behavior without changing source. Use @decorator syntax. Common: @property, @staticmethod, @classmethod.
Try/except/finally blocks catch exceptions. Specific exceptions first, generic last. Finally always executes. Custom exceptions inherit from Exception.
Object-Oriented Programming: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation. Re-usable, modular. Concepts: attributes, methods, constructors, access specifiers.
Inheritance: child class inherits from parent. Reuse code, specialize behavior. Single, multiple inheritance. Super() accesses parent methods.
Polymorphism: objects take multiple forms. Method overriding (child changes parent method), overloading (same name, different params). Benefits: flexibility, code reuse.
Encapsulation: bundling data and methods. Access control: public, private (prefix _), protected. Benefits: data safety, modularity.
SOLID: S (Single Responsibility), O (Open/Closed), L (Liskov Substitution), I (Interface Segregation), D (Dependency Inversion). Best practices for maintainable code.
Design patterns: reusable solutions to problems. Creational (Singleton, Factory), Structural (Adapter, Decorator), Behavioral (Observer, Strategy).
Mock: simulates object behavior. Replace external dependencies (API, database). Test isolation. Use unittest.mock. Verify calls, return values.
Unit testing: test individual functions/methods. Framework: pytest, unittest. Arrange (setup), Act (execute), Assert (verify). Each test independent.
Integration testing: test multiple components together. Verify APIs, database, external services. End-to-end scenarios. Tools: Selenium, REST frameworks.
Code coverage: percentage of code executed by tests. Tools: coverage.py (Python), Istanbul (JS). Target 70-80%. High coverage doesn't guarantee quality.
Linting: static analysis finding issues. Tools: pylint, flake8 (Python), ESLint (JS). Check: style, errors, potential bugs before runtime.
Practices: meaningful commits, branch per feature, code review, squash commits, semantic versioning. Clean history, easier debugging, collaboration.
DI: providing dependencies to class instead of creating internally. Benefits: testability, flexibility, loose coupling. Frameworks: Spring, dagger.
MVC: Model (data), View (UI), Controller (logic). Separates concerns. Model changes notify all views. Used in web frameworks: Django, Rails, ASP.NET.
Endpoint: URL + HTTP method. GET /users (read), POST /users (create), PUT /users/1 (update), DELETE /users/1 (delete). Status codes: 200, 201, 400, 404, 500.
2xx: Success (200, 201, 204). 3xx: Redirect (304, 307). 4xx: Client error (400, 401, 403, 404). 5xx: Server error (500, 502, 503).
GraphQL: query language for APIs. Single endpoint. Request only needed fields. Strongly typed schema. Alternative to REST. Tools: Apollo, GraphQL.js.
Type checking: verify variable types. Static (compile-time): TypeScript, mypy. Dynamic (runtime): Python, JavaScript. Benefits: catch errors early, documentation.
TypeScript: superset of JavaScript with types. Compiles to JavaScript. Features: interfaces, types, generics, decorators. IDE support, catch errors early.
Generics: write type-agnostic code. Syntax: <T>. Example: function identity<T>(x: T): T { return x; }. Reuse code, maintain type safety.
Null safety: prevent null pointer exceptions. Languages: Kotlin, TypeScript, Rust. Optional types, null checks. Better reliability.
Immutability: objects cannot change after creation. Benefits: thread-safe, predictable, functional programming. Languages: Rust (default), Scala, JavaScript (const).
FP: programming with functions, immutable data. Concepts: first-class functions, higher-order functions, pure functions, recursion. Languages: Haskell, Lisp, Scala.
Pure function: same input always gives same output, no side effects. Deterministic, testable, composable. No global state modifications.
Higher-order function: takes function as argument or returns function. Examples: map, filter, reduce. Enables functional composition, code reuse.
Recursion: function calls itself. Base case (stops), recursive case. Stack overflow risk with deep recursion. Solution: tail recursion, iteration.
Memoization: cache function results avoid recomputation. Trade-off: memory for speed. Used in DP, expensive computations. Python: @lru_cache decorator.
Big O: describes algorithm complexity. O(1) constant, O(log n) logarithmic, O(n) linear, O(n²) quadratic, O(2^n) exponential. Analyze scalability.
Space complexity: memory usage by algorithm. Exclude input. O(1) constant space, O(n) linear. Analysis similar to time complexity.
Amortized analysis: average cost over sequence operations. Example: dynamic array resize. O(1) amortized even though occasional O(n) operation.
Multiprocessing: multiple processes, truly parallel (bypass GIL). Use Process, Pool. Overhead due to IPC. For CPU-bound tasks.
Threading: multiple threads, share memory, not truly parallel (GIL). Use Thread, Lock, Condition. For I/O-bound tasks.
Async: single-threaded, concurrent execution. Callbacks, promises, async/await. Non-blocking I/O. Event loop manages. Python: asyncio, JavaScript.
Race condition: multiple threads access shared resource without synchronization. Data corruption, unpredictable behavior. Solution: locks, semaphores, atomic operations.
Deadlock: threads waiting forever for locks each other holds. Conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait. Prevention: ordering, timeouts.
GC: automatic memory management. Reference counting, mark-sweep, generational. Languages: Python, Java, Go. Trade-off: ease vs performance.
Memory leak: allocated memory not freed. Causes: unclosed resources, circular references, lost pointers. Detection: memory profilers, tools.
Pointer: variable storing memory address. C/C++ feature. Dereference: access value. Uses: dynamic allocation, passing by reference, data structures.
Value: copy object, independent. Reference: alias to object, share changes. Languages: C++ (both), Python (reference), JavaScript (reference).
Shallow copy: copies references, shares nested objects. Deep copy: recursively copies all objects. Use deepcopy() (Python) for nested structures.
Callback: function passed to another function, called later. Used in event handlers, async operations. Pyramid of doom problem with many nested callbacks.
WebSocket: bidirectional communication over single connection. Real-time apps: chat, notifications. Advantages: low latency vs HTTP polling.
Rate limiting: restrict requests per time. Prevents abuse, DDoS protection. Algorithms: token bucket, sliding window. Return 429 status.
Headers: Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified, Expires. Browser caches responses, reuses without fetching. RFC 7234 specifies caching rules.
CDN: Content Delivery Network. Globally distributed servers serve content from nearest location. Reduces latency, bandwidth, improves UX. Examples: CloudFlare, Akamai.
SSL/TLS: encryption for HTTPS. Handshake establishes secure connection. Certificates verify server identity. Protocol: TLS 1.3 latest.
Asymmetric: public key (encrypt), private key (decrypt). Slower than symmetric but enables PKI, digital signatures. Example: RSA.
Hash: convert input to fixed-size output. One-way, deterministic. Uses: passwords, checksums, hash tables. Algorithms: MD5 (broken), SHA-256, bcrypt.
Digital signature: prove authenticity, non-repudiation. Sign with private key, verify with public key. Uses: PKI, email, contracts.
PKI: system for creating, distributing, managing digital certificates. Authorities: CA, RA. Enables secure communication, establishes trust.
Regex: pattern for matching strings. Metacharacters: . * + ? ^ $ [ ] ( ) |. Tools: grep, sed, Python re module. Powerful but can be slow.
Documentation: describe endpoints, parameters, responses, errors. Tools: Swagger/OpenAPI, Postman, API Blueprint. Improves usability, reduces support burden.
Idempotent operation: multiple calls same result as one call. HTTP methods: GET, PUT, DELETE idempotent. POST not. Important for retries.
Stateless: no server-side state, scalable, each request independent. Stateful: server maintains state, session. REST API stateless, easier to scale.
Sessions: track user across requests. Session ID in cookie, stored on server/client. Alternatives: JWT (stateless), OAuth.
Cookie flags: Secure (HTTPS only), HttpOnly (no JS access), SameSite (CSRF protection). Domain, Path scope. Session cookies vs persistent.
Web scraping: extract data from websites. Tools: BeautifulSoup, Scrapy (Python). Respect robots.txt, terms. Uses: price monitoring, research.
Parse tree: represents syntactic structure. Root: start symbol. Derivation from grammar. Used in compilers, interpreters, NLP.
AST: simplified parse tree removing syntax nodes. More useful for interpretation. Used in: code analysis, refactoring, linting.
Compiler: translates to machine code before execution. Faster runtime. Interpreter: executes line by line. Slower but interactive. Python: bytecode interpreter.
JIT: Just-in-Time compilation. Compile hot code paths at runtime. Optimizations: inlining, loop optimization. Examples: Java HotSpot, V8 engine.
VM: emulates computer. Portable bytecode runs on any VM. JVM (Java), CLR (.NET), Python interpreter. Sandboxing, portability benefits.
Bytecode: intermediate representation. More efficient than source, interpreted faster. Examples: Java .class, Python .pyc. Stack-based or register-based.
Symbol table: maps identifiers to information. Lexical scope levels. Used in: type checking, code generation, optimization.
Linker: combines object files into executable. Resolves external references, allocates memory. Static linking (embedded), dynamic linking (shared libraries).
Loader: loads executable into memory. Relocates addresses, handles shared libraries. Dynamic loader handles runtime dependencies.
OS: manages hardware, provides services to programs. Functions: process management, memory, file system, I/O. Examples: Linux, Windows, macOS.
Synchronization: coordinate multiple processes. Tools: semaphores, mutex, monitors. Prevents race conditions, ensures mutual exclusion.
Context switch: save process state, load another. Overhead: register save/restore, cache miss. Frequency affects performance, responsiveness.
Algorithms for virtual memory: FIFO, LRU, Optimal. Replace page minimizing page faults. LRU most practical. Belady's anomaly with FIFO.
Demand paging: load pages on demand, not all upfront. Reduces memory usage. Page fault triggers load. Trade-off: latency vs efficient memory.
File system: organizes data hierarchy. Structures: FAT, NTFS, ext4. Features: permissions, links, journaling. Balances performance, reliability, capacity.
Inode: stores file metadata. Contains: permissions, owner, size, timestamps, pointers. Direct/indirect blocks point to file data.
Permissions: read (r), write (w), execute (x) for owner, group, others. Octal notation: 755. Prevents unauthorized access.
